item.title: How Jason and Nick Robertson Nearly Formed Brotherly Duo With Penguins
item.description: How Jason and Nick Robertson Nearly Formed Brotherly Duo With Penguins originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Like many multi-million and billion-dollar entities, the Penguins have postured themselves as a family for the better part of six decades. Their history suggests that label isn't entirely inaccurate. Pittsburgh's roster has housed an impressive number of brother pairings, from Doug and Greg Brown and Chris and Peter Ferraro to Mario and Alain Lemieux (for one game). For a fleeting moment during the offseason, it appeared that they might have added another. After landing Nick Robertson in a trade with the Maple Leafs, the Penguins turned their sights to his high-profile brother, Jason Robertson. Those plans didn't quite come to fruition. But all hope is not lost just yet. With that, here's what you need to know about Pittsburgh's pursuit of Jason Robertson — aided in no small part by its decision to acquire his younger brother, Nick. MORE: Jaromir Jagr Teases Career Decision After 38th Professional Season How Jason and Nick Robertson Nearly Formed Brotherly Duo With Penguins The elder Robertson was linked heavily with Pittsburgh in the offseason. The Stars standout commanded significant interest from the Penguins, with general manager Kyle Dubas believed to have attempted to lodge a trade offer at Dallas, according to The Athletic's Josh Yohe. Pittsburgh's acquisition of the younger Robertson via trade with the Maple Leafs figured to improve its bargaining position. The Stars were known to be in talks with teams over a potential swap for Jason, who hit restricted free agency after the 2025-26 season ended. They even agreed to a deal with the Kraken that would have sent the No. 7 pick and assets to Dallas in exchange for Jason Robertson. However, the deal was nixed at the 11th hour after Jason refused signing a long-term extension to stay in Seattle. Jason would eventually ink a one-year, $12 million deal to stay with the Stars for the 2026-27 season. Dallas has been known to covet agreeing terms to a longer-term deal with the winger, who has produced 516 points in 478 games. The Stars offered him a qualifying offer prior to the start of free agency. If they opted against matching a bid on him by other teams, they would have secured draft-pick compensation — four first-round selections for a player of Robertson's projected value. His contractual situation — Robertson will hit unrestricted free agency at the end of the season, meaning Dallas stands to lose him for nothing if he decides to go elsewhere — could force the Stars to deal him at the trade deadline if they feel he's leaning towards leaving the team at the end of the year. Nick's arrival could improve Pittsburgh's chances of attracting Jason, one of the sport's most dynamic forwards. Any movement involving Jason Robertson will take place in the new year. item.title: Napoli Interested in Sassuolo Loanee and Young Goalie
item.description: Napoli Interested in Sassuolo Loanee and Young Goalie Napoli have recently rekindled interest in Sebastiano Esposito, whom they tracked extensively last summer before Sassuolo snapped him up late after he had a falling out with Cagliari. The Azzurri settled for giving Lorenzo Lucca and Noa Lang another chance after their loan spells. According to Alfredo Pedullà , the Neroverdi beat Torino and Genoa in the race, bringing the striker in temporarily with a €1M fee and a €11M option to buy. If the Partenopei offloaded their misfits, he’d be among their top targets to replenish their attack thanks to his versatility. Sassuolo aren’t in good shape in the standings and would like to keep Esposito, so Napoli would have to table a very persuasive offer, Corriere dello Sport relays. In addition to searching for new weapons, their director Giovanni Manna recently met with the entourage of Coritiba goalie Pedro Morisco. The Azzurri could accelerate their plans to add a new shot-stopper. Alex Meret just suffered a fifth vertebra fracture that will sideline him for at least two months. Moreover, his contract is up at the end of the season, and Vanja Milinkovic-Savic hasn’t been entirely convincing. The 22-year-old represented the national team twice with Carlo Ancelotti at the helm. He has kept 44 clean sheets and conceded 107 goals in 113 matches with his club. Our Take on Napoli, Esposito, and Morisco It’s not great that they’re linked to other attackers shortly after meeting with Gustavo Varela’s agent , although they’re pretty different, and the Sassuolo man would pair up better with Rasmus Hojlund. The deal is technically difficult but not impossible if they are willing to spend. At some point, they’ll have to choose between the sticks, and the answer might not be one of their current options.

item.title: Iga Swiatek tipped to be a real ‘dark horse’ on the WTA Tour in 2027 by Serena Williams’ ex-coach
item.description: Iga Swiatek will want to get back to competing for Grand Slams once again in 2027 after a largely disappointing 2026 season. Though there were some high points, most notably her triumph at the Canadian Open, this season was a difficult one for Swiatek , who had won at least one Grand Slam each year from 2022 to 2025. That streak came to an end this year, with the Pole reaching just one major quarterfinal at the Australian Open before bowing out of Roland Garros, Wimbledon and the US Open early. Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images Rick Macci previews Iga Swiatek’s 2027 season on the WTA Tour Swiatek has confirmed her first tournament of the 2027 season will be the Brisbane International, and Serena Williams’ former coach, Rick Macci, has high expectations for the 25-year-old ahead of her trip to Australia. In a post on X , formerly known as Twitter, Macci said: “The Polish Punisher is my dark horse in 2027. With all her current weapons (speed, quickness angles fight grit proven and groovin) and even if her effective but limited serve stays the same(hope not) the wildcard for the Punisher is what happens After each point between her ears will determine if Iga finds a few more gears.” In another post, Macci said: “Iga should go into the lab and experiment like never before. Off the ground she is ok and sound. Just discussions on certain moments in combat as most coaches have said that. If her mindset is steady and loving the battle the Punisher is hard to rattle. “But in the off-season, everything is on the table with the serve and see if they can rewire and change a nerve. Experiment with grip stance takeback pinpoint platform power position ball toss hip and elbow angles to get more easy power and location but her legs have to drive the racquet IN at the proper time to get the optimal external and internal shoulder rotation.” Swiatek finished the 2026 season ranked ninth in the world, having started the year second.

item.title: Tom Brady calls out NFL players for extravagant touchdown celebrations
item.description: Former NFL quarterback Tom Brady is taking aim at today’s players, criticizing the elaborate touchdown celebrations that have become increasingly popular across the league. During a recent appearance on Fox Sports’ weekly ‘ Ask Tom ‘ segment, the seven-time Super Bowl champion shared his frustration with the amount of choreography players put into their end zone celebrations. “I’ve seen more choreography in some of these touchdown celebrations than in a Broadway show, learn your assignments, how about that,” Brady said. A little more playbook, a little less Broadway, if you ask @TomBrady. https://t.co/HCj7BQz5h2 — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 20, 2026 The legendary quarterback specifically referenced the Detroit Lions’ controversial celebration during their international game in Munich, Germany, which quickly became a talking point around the league. Brady questioned how players can remember elaborate routines while occasionally struggling with fundamental responsibilities on the field. item.title: Over 12 Teams Reportedly Trying To Sign Freddy Peralta; Cubs, Padres, Rays Included
item.description: Free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta Freddy Peralta is one of the best players available in free agency this year, and while all of the headlines are about Tarik Skubal, Peralta is reportedly drawing plenty of interest. There are still over a half a dozen teams in play for Peralta with the Padres, both Chicago teams and believe it or not the Rays all still involved and maybe the Braves too but the latter not confirmed," wrote MLB insider Jim Bowden on X on Friday. "Other teams are in the periphery but not as aggressive. It's getting late and time for teams to pick it up or lose out." Peralta is a two-time All-Star who had an up-and-down season. He struggled with the New York Mets, but thrived with the Tampa Bay Rays after the trade deadline. On the Rays, he had a 3.25 ERA in 10 regular season starts, posting a 0.79 ERA in his final six regular season starts. In the postseason, he logged a 1.08 ERA through his first four outings and was even named the American League Championship Series MVP. His final postseason start came against the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series and he allowed five runs in 4 2/3 innings of work. Peralta was a great pitcher for the Brewers in the first eight seasons of his career. He lost his way in Queens, but the Rays helped him find himself again. He is set up for a nine-figure payday as a free agent, but may have to wait for Skubal to sign to get his best offers. item.title: U15s face Santos at Vila Belmiro in Paulista semi-final second leg
item.description: U15s face Santos at Vila Belmiro in Paulista semi-final second leg This Saturday, the Under-15s face Santos at 9 a.m. at Vila Belmiro in Santos, São Paulo, in the second leg of the Campeonato Paulista semifinals for their age group. Led by coach Vinícius dos Santos, the team has put together a solid Campeonato Paulista campaign. They finished top of their group in both of the first two stages, recording 14 wins, three draws and just one defeat, with 68 goals scored and ten conceded. As the competition progressed, the Tricolor got past AA Flamengo in the third stage after a 1-1 away draw and a 3-0 win in Cotia. In the round of 16, they eliminated Guarani with a 5-0 home rout and a 1-1 draw in Campinas. In the quarterfinals, they overcame Palmeiras: after drawing the first leg 2-2, they came from behind to win 2-1 at Arena Crefisa Barueri. In the first leg of the semifinals, played at CFA Laudo Natel in Cotia, the Tricolor beat Santos 1-0 thanks to a goal from Enzo Henrique. With that advantage, the team need only a draw in the return leg at Vila Belmiro to secure a place in the state championship final. A defeat by a one-goal margin would send the tie to a penalty shootout. So far, they have played 25 matches, with 18 wins, six draws and just one defeat. They have scored 83 goals and conceded 14. Under-14s In the afternoon, the Under-14s return to action against Guarani at 2:30 p.m. at CFA Laudo Natel in Cotia, São Paulo, for the second leg of the Campeonato Paulista semifinal. In the first leg, played last Sunday at Estádio Brinco de Ouro da Princesa in Campinas, São Paulo, the Tricolor won 2-0 with goals from center-backs Guilherme Barbosa and Estevão, taking the lead in the battle for a place in the final. item.title: Chelsea fined £150,000 for discriminatory chanting
item.description: [Getty Images] Chelsea have been fined £150,000 by the Football Association as part of a punishment for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chants during an FA Cup third-round win at Charlton Athletic in January. The club have also been warned about their future conduct and had an action plan imposed on them in relation to the offence. "Chelsea FC failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way with either an express or implied reference to religion or belief," said an FA statement. Chelsea admitted the charge but had an appeal against the fine issued by an independent regulatory commission rejected. The FA's written reasons stated that although the discriminatory chanting "lasted approximately one minute and was not repeated, the scale of participation was a significant aggravating feature". "We unequivocally condemn this behaviour," said a Chelsea statement. "Sectarian abuse - chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group - and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club. "Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary." The FA itself was fined by Uefa for a similar incident of chanting, from England's away support during their Nations League victory in Spain on Sunday. item.title: The Chicago Bears Can’t Afford To Overlook the Saints
item.description: The Chicago Bears have spent the first half of the season proving they belong among the NFC’s contenders. Now, coming out of their bye week with a 7-2 record and four consecutive victories, Chicago faces a different challenge: avoiding a setback against an opponent it is expected to beat. The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday’s matchup at Soldier Field with a 3-6 record, but their struggles shouldn’t give Chicago a reason to relax. With a Thanksgiving showdown against the Detroit Lions approaching, the Bears have an opportunity to build momentum before entering one of the most demanding stretches of their season. Chicago has shown it can survive mistakes, but Sunday’s matchup offers a chance to demonstrate something equally important. The Bears need to show they can control a game without relying on another dramatic finish. Ben Johnson on the NFC North Competition: "Doesn't matter right now. Once again, it's all about winning this week, so we'll worry about everything else when it's time. It's not time for that. Caleb Williams threw a career-high four interceptions, repeatedly giving Tampa Bay opportunities to erase Chicago’s early advantage. Those interceptions weren’t all the result of the same problem. According to the Chicago Sun-Times , Williams acknowledged forcing his first interception toward Rome Odunze in the end zone. Tampa Bay’s pressure contributed to two more poor decisions, while his fourth interception came on a pass tipped at the line of scrimmage. The distinction matters because New Orleans possesses a defensive front capable of creating similar problems. Chase Young and Carl Granderson have combined for 16.5 sacks, giving the Saints two dangerous edge rushers who can disrupt Williams’ timing and force him outside the pocket. Williams cannot afford to let pressure dictate his decision-making. Throwing the football away when a play breaks down and taking available underneath completions would let Chicago maintain possession rather than give New Orleans more opportunities. Despite the turnovers, Williams remains confident in his approach. “I’m going to keep gripping it and keep ripping it,” Williams told reporters following the Tampa Bay victory. That confidence is important, but Chicago needs better decisions to go with it. The Saints have recorded just four interceptions this season, presenting Williams with an opportunity to rebound against a secondary that has struggled to generate takeaways. item.title: Hawks Hits: Costly Slow Start, But Offense Was Capable Without Bedard
item.description: For the fifth time in seven games without captain Connor Bedard this season, the Chicago Blackhawks offense failed to reach three goals in Thursday’s 4-2 loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets . The Blackhawks couldn’t claw their way back from an early 2-0 deficit, with a slow start proving costly in the team’s lone regulation loss of the four-game homestand, finishing 2-1-1. Facing a Columbus team that entered the United Center on the back of five straight losses, with only eight goals during that stretch, it was particularly disappointing that the Hawks were giving up the better chances and losing most of the puck battles and foot races in the early going. The Blue Jackets led 17-7 in shots on goal in the first period and were ahead 22-10 at the game’s midway point, with Cam Talbot not having to do much to maintain the two-goal lead, which the Blackhawks could never overcome. “After a couple good games here, coming up against a team that we know we should beat, giving them the edge to win that game, that’s the difference-maker.” Frank Nazar said after the game. Head coach Jeff Blashill was “extremely” frustrated with the lack of compete, urgency, and execution in the first half, three things he and his players always talk about in the locker room in between periods. “For me, it was not good enough, not good enough, not good enough,” Blashill said, referencing the three aspects. “So then, don’t even talk about X’s and O’s at that point. We weren’t skating. We’re a pressure team. If you don’t skate, you’re a step behind all over the ice. I thought we were really soft with the puck in our own end… and I thought our execution was poor.” After carving his team a bit, Blashill ended that statement by crediting them for not going down without a fight and improving their play over the second half. Over the final 30 minutes, the offense started figuring out how to generate scoring chances without their star player. Despite Bedard’s absence, the power play converted for the fourth straight game, with Frank Nazar netting his team-leading 11th goal of the season in the second period. Still trailing by two entering the third, the Blackhawks were pressing hard and cut the deficit to one again with a snipe from Cole Smith with 16:08 remaining. But even though several players had quality looks to even the score, the equalizer never came, with Talbot hanging tough to keep the Jackets ahead. The Blackhawks outchanced Columbus 10-2 in the finale frame, as Roman Kantserov, Ryan Donato , Ryan Greene, Tyler Bertuzzi , Sam Rinzel , and Nazar each had an opportunity for the game-tying tally. item.description: Mikel Arteta sends message to Arsenal board over next contract deal Arsenal Want Martin Odegaard Contract Sorted as Arteta Makes His Position Clear Arsenal are moving methodically on contracts and the next obvious file on the desk is Martin Odegaard. Mikel Arteta has said it plainly enough. He wants his captain tied down for the long term, because in his view this is not a marginal player or a symbolic armband holder. This is one of the central pieces. The club have already pushed ahead with fresh agreements for key members of their Premier League-winning squad. Declan Rice, David Raya and Jurrien Timber are understood to have agreed terms in recent weeks, while Piero Hincapie has also landed an improved deal. Add that to earlier commitments from Bukayo Saka, William Saliba and Arteta himself, and the strategy is clear. Arsenal are trying to lock in stability before uncertainty has a chance to develop. Arteta sees Odegaard as critical Odegaard’s current contract runs until 2028, but he is edging towards the final 18 months. In modern football that matters. Leave it too long and the conversation changes. It stops being about control and starts being about leverage. Arteta has no interest in ambiguity here. “Martin is an instrumental player for us, for me,” Arteta said. He then expanded on why. “I think what he’s done for the club and for the team in the last years since he joined has just been [on] an uplifted trajectory with some moments of incredible consistency and magic, and some others that are a bit more difficult. Photo IMAGO “But I think his role and my opinion on how important he is to continue to do what we’re doing is critical.” When asked directly whether he wanted Odegaard to remain beyond the current deal, the answer was brief and definitive: “Yes, definitely yes.” Martin Odegaard contract talks still waiting The awkward part is that Odegaard himself said over the international break that talks have not yet started. That stands out when so many team-mates have already progressed or concluded their own negotiations. It does not automatically signal a problem, but it does invite questions. Arteta, predictably, would not open that door. “You know that I never talk about these things,” Arteta said. “I can tell you the opinion I have and I think that’s a very general and unanimous feeling that we have, everyone at the club.” That is standard manager language, but the message underneath it is obvious enough. item.title: 'Right time' for Smith exit - but Murray not ready for role
item.description: Leon Smith was Andy Murray's childhood coach before taking over as Britain's Davis Cup captain in 2010 [Getty Images] Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" to leave the role after almost 17 years - although Andy Murray is not ready to replace him. Smith was appointed in 2010 and guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936. The 50-year-old Scot's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible. Former world number one Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this stage. Since retiring in 2024, Murray has been enjoying spending more time with his family and working on business interests, as well as coaching Novak Djokovic and now Jack Draper on a part-time basis. "He obviously is the standout candidate, isn't he?" said Smith. "I do hope it's something he does in the future, but I respect that it's not for him right now, and I can understand it. "But I really hope at some point in the future that he does take it on." Smith said he had been pondering his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna. "There comes a time whether it is personally you need a change, or it is good for the team to have something else," said Smith, who seemed emotional in a video call with reporters. Leon Smith guided Great Britain to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years [Getty Images] "I've done it for a very long time and I think there are others who will enjoy the role and can bring something different to the role. "I love the role and haven't lost any passion for it. But it feels like the right time for me personally and the guys moving forwards." With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign. Murray, 39, was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career. "He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said. "I've obviously known Leon a long time. I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. "I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain." Smith, who will continue in his role as head of British men's tennis, took over almost 17 years ago with the team in danger of being relegated to the lowest tier of the Davis Cup. item.title: Kevin De Bruyne: Napoli express desire to keep player in January
item.description: Kevin De Bruyne: Napoli express desire to keep player in January Serie A side Napoli have been facing a real possibility of losing Kevin De Bruyne in January but they are expected to stand firm in a decision to keep him at the Partenopei. Corriere dello Sport report that PSV have tried to make in-roads over a deal for January but Aurelio de Laurentiis issued a firm ‘no’ to their offer. This is mainly because the club do not want to sell in the winter and even Max Allegri sees him as a lynchpin for the side. But that doesn’t rule out a summer exit, though. De Bruyne’s current deal runs out at the end of the campaign and PSV remain in the hunt. They can now decide to reach an agreement for a deal in the summer, having spoken to the Belgian’s entourage extensively. It is believed their initial plan was to execute a summer deal and they simply wanted to assess the idea of bringing it forward. They have now gone back to their initial plan, as they try to determine whether Napoli will hand him an extension or not. Most importantly, they will rely on the player’s wishes to return closer home to seal a deal and hope that this convinces his entourage. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: Rams receiver Nacua out two months after knee surgery
item.description: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay, left, says Rams receiver Puka Nacua, right, will be sidelined for a couple of months after undergoing left knee surgery (Dustin Satloff) Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent right knee ligament surgery this week and could miss the remainder of the NFL season, Rams coach Sean McVay said on Friday. Nacua will miss "a couple of months" after the operation, McVay said, a timetable that might allow the 25-year-old pass-catcher to return for the playoffs if the Rams (6-4) qualify. On Thursday, Nacua was suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy in an incident last December. Nacua was already set to miss at least the next three games for the Rams after being placed on injured reserve a week ago with knee and toe injuries suffered in a victory over Washington on November 8. Nacua, in his fourth NFL campaign after being taken by the Rams in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft, led the league in receptions last season with 129. The Arizona Cardinals are not having a good 2026 season, but it's hardly a surprise given where the team is at as a franchise. But part of the issue isn't just the struggles of the roster; it's the injuries this offense has faced. Gardner Minshew, Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, and Jeremiyah Love are all out for an extended period of time. Only Love might be back at some point this season. Carson Beck is throwing to a lackluster supporting cast. But now even he is banged up. After popping up on the injury report on Thursday with a back injury, Beck, according to a report from Theo Mackie of AZ Central Sports , is not looking likely to play in Week 11 against the Kansas City Chiefs . Cardinals not likely to have Carson Beck for Week 11 matchup "Carson Beck will not practice today and the Cardinals will 'proceed' as if Josh Johnson will start on Sunday," Mackie reports. "They're not closing the door on Beck, but it seems unlikely that he'll play." Beck went on the injury report on Thursday with a back injury, putting his status for Week 11 in doubt. That doubt now appears to be close to a certainty, as the expectation is Beck will be ruled out for the Chiefs game. Arizona will now be down to their fourth quarterback this season, as Jacoby Brissett has been traded to the Baltimore Ravens , Minshew and Beck are hurt, and now Josh Johnson is set to take over. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day The 3-7 Cardinals are going up against the 7-2 Chiefs in Week 11, in what's looking like a near-insurmountable matchup. Down to QB4 on the season with a lackluster supporting cast is far from ideal. While Beck played poorly in his NFL debut, going 11 of 18 passing for 108 yards and two picks with no touchdowns, it's still a big blow to lose Beck for Week 11. He's not yet ruled out, but Cardinals fans should anticipate missing out on Beck for Week 11 against the Chiefs, with a return in Week 12 or Week 13 against the Washington Commanders or Philadelphia Eagles more likely to be Beck's second NFL start. item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 28: Gavin McKenna #92 of the Toronto Maple Leafs looks on during the first period against the Seattle Kraken at Climate Pledge Arena on October 28, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Toronto Maple Leafs rookie Gavin McKenna is clearly still figuring life out in the NHL. But, that being said, he possesses a skill set that very few NHLers seem to have. The 18-year-old phenom is a wizard with the puck on his stick, and he’s shown that early in his NHL career with a quietly impressive six goals and 14 points in 24 games. Even though he’s shown an ability to produce early, Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller seems unwilling to put him in the situation that would best utilize his skill set. Jim Hiller Explains Why Gavin McKenna Isn’t Playing in Overtime The Maple Leafs have gone to overtime three times this season, but McKenna hasn’t played a single shift in the extra frame. That continued Thursday against Los Angeles, when Hiller instead leaned on Auston Matthews, William Nylander, John Tavares, Easton Cowan and Jack Roslovic. Speaking to reporters after the loss, Hiller acknowledged that McKenna’s offensive talent doesn’t necessarily guarantee him an opportunity in three-on-three situations. “I don’t really evaluate his 5-on-5 play into 3-on-3,” Hiller said, via Maple Leafs Hotstove . “3-on-3, it’s just a different game in the NHL.” Jim Hiller on why Gavin Mckenna is yet to play a shift in overtime this season. 🤔 pic.twitter.com/uhdRcjkpEB — BarDown (@BarDown) November 20, 2026 The coach also revealed that McKenna has come close to getting an opportunity, only to be called back to the bench. “He’s watched. We’ve had him up and then called him off,” Hiller explained. Hiller suggested that protecting McKenna’s confidence is part of the decision. “I just want to make sure he’s ready for that,” Hiller said. But, the decision becomes harder to justify as the Leafs season continues to slip away. item.title: SMU’s Texas-Sized Bet on Lacrosse
item.description: High school senior lacrosse standout Trystean Warburton grew up supporting his hometown school of SMU, often visiting the campus and rooting for the football program. But he never thought he could play college lacrosse there, let alone anywhere in his home state of Texas, which had zero NCAA Division I teams. But on Oct. 15, SMU announced the launch of the first D-I men’s lacrosse program, which will play in the highly competitive ACC beginning in 2028. Warburton, a four-star face-off specialist, flipped his Lehigh commitment almost immediately. “I loved [Lehigh]. I loved the coaching staff over there,” Warburton tells Front Office Sports . “But I always heard talks about the SMU program possibly being added to D-I, and I didn’t know if it was going to be really added into D-I during my years of playing. But I always dreamt of coming to SMU.” At a time when schools nationwide are considering cutting sports, SMU has found itself in the perfect position to start one—and hit the ground running. It has generous donors pouring millions into the program, already enabling it to poach an inaugural head coach with a championship pedigree; a state with an exploding interest in lacrosse, but a vacuum at the college level; and a new NCAA eligibility rule allowing it to build a roster that can compete for a D-I championship in Year 1. “Things just kind of came together,” SMU AD Damon Evans tells FOS. “Coupled with the fundraising, coupled with our founders, coupled with the interest [in Texas] … we just found that there was just so much coming together to allow us to get to the point where we are today.” Off to the Races The cash to stand up the Mustangs program flooded in quickly. On launch day, SMU announced it’d already secured a $15 million commitment. Evans says that war chest has swelled to $20 million to date, getting closer to the fundraising goal of $25 million. Chief among those donors are Gary and Sylvie Crum, whose fortune comes largely from investment management. The existing club lacrosse facility at SMU—infrastructure that has allowed the Mustangs to seamlessly step into varsity play—is named the Crum Lacrosse and Sports Field. (One of the main conference rooms in the USA Lacrosse headquarters in Maryland is also named after the family.) About two weeks after the launch, SMU announced it had hired Princeton offensive coordinator Jim Mitchell, the architect of the attack that propelled the Tigers to the 2026 national championship. In an October statement, Mitchell said: “The opportunity to build Texas’ first Division I men’s lacrosse program from the ground up, in a city like Dallas and a conference like the ACC, is something truly special. The expectation is to compete at the highest level, and I can’t wait to get started.” The NCAA’s new eligibility rule also “accelerated” the launch, Evans says. item.title: Shohei Ohtani signs lifetime deal with New Balance, plans changes to cleats
item.description: Shohei Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers will likely take him through the end of his playing career. Now, Ohtani has a career-long endorsement deal with his longtime sportswear provider to go along with it. Ohtani agreed to a new contract with New Balance that will last through the end of his baseball career, as he told GQ in a story published on Friday. It is believed to be the first such lifetime sponsorship deal for a baseball player, putting Ohtani alongside the likes of other superstar athletes such as LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo (with Nike) and Damian Lillard (with Adidas) to strike such a commitment. Los Angeles Dodgers Shohei Ohtani walks to the plate against the Atlanta Braves during the NLDS in Los Angeles, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. Wally Skalij for the CA Post “There’s a lot of trust,” Ohtani told GQ through an interpreter. “We’ve obviously built friendships, as well. They’ve been able to accommodate my requests, the things I’ve asked for, and, like I said, that takes the involvement of a lot of trust. That relationship has been very, very good and smooth. I had no reservations about extending our relationship.” Ohtani has been the face of New Balance’s baseball line since originally signing a long-term endorsement deal with the company in 2023. item.title: Will MLB copy the Brewers? Their World Series title could reshape hitting philosophies
item.description: It's been less than a month since the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers accomplished something that for years felt inevitable and impossible: the first World Series title in franchise history. Surely, crumpled Miller Lite cans and loose strips of confetti from the parade still remain in the nooks and crannies of downtown Milwaukee. Hundreds of thousands of Wisconsinites had their love of baseball strengthened, reaffirmed, validated. The impact of that Brewers run could eventually stretch far beyond Badger State borders. Major League Baseball is a copycat league in a copycat world. Success fosters emulation, winning precipitates mimicry. The 2026 Brewers — the lineup in particular — were such a different beast from other recent champions that it's reasonable to expect that other teams might attempt to mirror various aspects of Milwaukee's strategic DNA. During the regular season, Milwaukee led baseball in several offensive categories, some traditionally considered conducive to scoring runs, others, not so much. The Brewers boasted the lowest chase rate in MLB at 26.8% and, accordingly, the highest walk rate (10.6%). That's an obvious recipe for success, a tale as old as time, or at least the Moneyball A's. See pitches, draw walks, be patient, get ahead in counts and you'll force pitchers to feed you more juicy pitches to hit. Milwaukee was also prolific at producing batted balls to the opposite field (league-leading 29.4%) and on the ground (48.1%). They ranked dead last in MLB in "pull air percentage" at 12.4%. The Chicago Cubs, the only club to score more runs than Milwaukee in 2026, led all of baseball in pull air percentage with a 21.5% mark. Milwaukee bulldozed its way to the title that included an NLCS sweep and a gentleman's sweep in the World Series. Erick W. Rasco via Getty Images It's worth noting that over the last decade, the league has experienced a dramatic increase in pull air percentage, from 14.9 in 2015 to 18.4 in 2026. That's in line with contemporary hitting philosophy. Power (and the corresponding runs and riches) comes in the air. For most players, that slug is easier to come by to the pull side. From Justin Turner to pre-falloff Chris Davis to Cal Raleigh to Kyle Schwarber to Isaac Paredes, we've seen time and time again that learning to pull the baseball with authority leads to good results. The Brewers, to a certain extent, bucked that trend and did so proudly. Accolades and earnings usually come via power production. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
